title: messaging: a default (fallback) value for an email or notify template hole, so a missing variable does not print as empty text
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

## Source

From HotCRM card objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2431, landed as hotcrm#2433. The maintainer agreed to filing this card at **p2** (2026-11-12T09:47Z).

## The gap (measured on @objectstack 18.3.0)

- plugin-email's `render()` fills a `{{path}}` hole, or prints `""` when the value is missing. It takes one formatter per hole and has no default or conditional.
- The messaging `interpolate()` behaves the same way.
- The formula package's hole judge says to do any branching "in the caller that supplies the data".

So a template cannot say "use X, or else Y".

## Why it matters

- hotcrm#2433 changed six shipped templates to read `{{person_name}}`, and the four shipped flows pass it.
- A self-hosted customer's own flow may send one of these templates with only `first_name` and `last_name`, the variables it was written against. Its notice then prints an empty name, and nothing warns anyone.

## What would close it

- A default in the hole syntax, for example `{{person_name | default: first_name}}` or a literal fallback.
- Or a diagnostic when a template is rendered without a variable it names.

## hotcrm half

None now. The residue is stated in hotcrm#2433's changeset.
